title: Tax-Loss Selling Candidate Universe
purpose: Define the minimum survivorship-aware equity candidate dataset needed before testing whether large tax-year losers experience late-year pressure and early-year rebound.
data_grain: daily equity universe with year-to-date return, liquidity, spread, and tax-calendar labels
candidate_sources: daily adjusted OHLCV vendor data with delisted symbols when available
exchange listing and delisting files or vendor security master
high-low spread proxy from daily bars when quoted spread is unavailable
tax-calendar definitions for late-year candidate selection and early-year rebound windows
construction_rules: Select candidates using only information available before the rebound window.
Define late-year selection dates and early-year holding windows before inspecting returns.
Keep delisted symbols and failed securities in the universe when they were tradable at selection time.
Separate size and liquidity buckets before any performance summary.
Do not tune loser thresholds after seeing January or rebound returns.
Record whether each symbol had corporate actions, mergers, or delistings that could distort adjusted-price behavior.
quality_checks: Every candidate must have a valid year_to_date_return computed from adjusted prices available at the selection date.
Every tested symbol must have pre-selection liquidity and spread estimates.
Missing post-selection prices must be classified as delisting, acquisition, halt, or data gap before exclusion.
The universe must include non-survivors or clearly mark survivorship bias as a blocking limitation.
No candidate threshold may be derived from later rebound returns.
Tax-year labels and trading windows must be deterministic and independent of returns.
minimum_viable_tests: No-trade cohort study comparing severe losers, moderate losers, and non-losers across late-year and early-year windows.
Separate summaries by size and liquidity bucket before any aggregate conclusion.
Cost sensitivity using spread or conservative bps assumptions before any executable strategy.
Year-by-year stability check across multiple tax years.
A single fixed candidate-threshold and holding-window strategy only after the cohort diagnostic identifies a plausible direction.
known_limitations: Free public data is usually survivorship-biased and may be unsuitable for this mechanism.
Daily bars cannot identify taxable ownership, actual tax-loss harvesting, or intraday execution quality.
Small-cap and delisted-security data can be expensive, messy, and legally constrained by vendor licenses.
Corporate actions, mergers, and bankruptcies may dominate returns for the worst losers.
The current backtester does not model market impact or position-size limits from thin liquidity.
next_action: Find a survivorship-aware equity universe source, or explicitly downgrade tax-loss selling to blocked if only current-survivor price data is available.
